        "scope_text": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who meets all specified statutory criteria.",

        "logic_text": "(1) Has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) Has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave ( see § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees), and (3) Is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",

        "statement": "An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (noting § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.)."

      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F006"],
        "scope_text": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",

        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation (38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq.), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (such as for education or childrearing purposes)."

unit_attributes.scope_text: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who meets all specified statutory criteria.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.logic_text: (1) Has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) Has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave ( see § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees), and (3) Is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (noting § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: For the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer.
unit_attributes.logic_text: need not be consecutive months, provided
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.logic_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee has had a break in service of more than seven years and either the break was occasioned by USERRA-covered service or a written agreement exists concerning rehire.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.logic_text: must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) ... ; or (ii) ...
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation (38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq.), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (such as for education or childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when an employee has an absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.logic_text: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must be also counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Under this section with respect to USERRA-covered service obligations.
unit_attributes.logic_text: However, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA
unit_attributes.statement: This section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.).
unit_attributes.logic_text: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (such as sick or vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.logic_text: 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.logic_text: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.logic_text: However, if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
